MCP Console lets your agent explore data and develop code interactively in R, Python, and SQL.

Code runs in an [OS-level sandbox](SANDBOX.md) by default.
Console prepares environments and packages automatically; no Console configuration file is required.

Console works with MCP-compatible clients such as Codex and Claude Code and does not depend on a particular model provider.
You can also use Console from [R](R.md) or [Python](PYTHON.md).

::: {.home-links}
[Get started](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Build on Console](BUILD.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [Reference](REFERENCE.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

Console provides a unified API across macOS, Linux, and Windows x64.
It is currently a **development preview**.

## Work iteratively

Console gives agents the interactive affordances of a REPL, so they can work iteratively: run code, inspect results, and decide what to try next.
They can refine plots, read help, respond to interactive prompts, and step through code in a debugger.
Long computations can keep running between calls, and agents can interrupt work or restart an unresponsive session.

The environment is designed for agents, with help and output formatted for them.
For example, Console collapses progress bar redraws and previews large results to keep them from flooding the model's context.
The agent can then inspect those results in more detail without rerunning the computation.

## Use one language or combine them {#one-workspace-three-languages}

Console embeds R, Python, and DuckDB in the same process.
The agent can switch between R, Python, and SQL on any turn, choosing the language and libraries that make each task easiest or most efficient.
It can reuse live data and models across languages without exporting and reloading intermediate files.

[Reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/) connects R and Python, and [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) can query in-memory data frames as SQL views.

R and Python can each run without the other.

See [Sessions and languages](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md) for examples, database connections, and plots.

## Use a full runtime in a sandbox {#status-and-trust}

Console uses native R and Python runtimes, with access to their package ecosystems, including packages with compiled code.
An OS-level sandbox enforces limits on file and network access.

The default `read_only` sandbox profile restricts network access and filesystem writes.
You can customize these permissions to allow writes to selected paths, block reads from selected paths, and control network access with domain allowlists or denylists.
See [Sandbox and trust](SANDBOX.md) for the defaults and how to adapt them to your work.

<span id="run-commands-in-a-sandbox"></span>

The [`mcp-console sandbox` subcommand](SANDBOX_COMMAND.md) makes the same sandbox available for scripts and other programs, independently of an agent session.
The permissions apply to the command and its child processes.

```sh
mcp-console sandbox -- python analysis.py
```

## Use packages without managing environments {#environment-setup}

Console automatically prepares its own environments and package libraries, reusing cached installations across sessions.
You don't need to create an environment or install packages for the agent.

The agent can request packages from the full R and Python ecosystems as an analysis develops, without requiring approval for each package.
By default, these requests are handled in a separate OS-level sandbox, with writes limited to dependency caches and temporary directories and network access limited to allowed package and tooling hosts.
Installing a package doesn't expand the permissions of the agent's code.

See [Packages and environments](REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Review the agent's work

[Recordings](RECORDING.md) retain code, output, and plots so you can see what the agent ran in Console and inspect the results.
They also provide a starting point for reproducible analyses and reports.

## Build on Console {#build-on-console}

Replace the complete tool description and instructions, choose which language interfaces and parameters the model can use, and preconfigure the runtime.
Set sandbox permissions to control access to files and networks.

For example, build a data chat with only SQL and a selected database connection, or a reporting assistant with a prepared R or Python environment.

[Build on Console](BUILD.md) introduces tool customization, prepared sessions, and the R and Python clients.

## Where Console fits

- **Unattended analysis:** run long analyses with limits on filesystem writes and network access.
- **Model evaluations:** evaluate how an agent explores data, checks its work, and responds to results.
- **Conversational exploration:** discuss questions and results while the agent works in its own session.
- **Large datasets:** keep data and intermediate results in memory for follow-up questions.
- **Debugging and package development:** pause execution and inspect live objects where a failure occurs.
